title: BottomTabBar
wrapsNative: TabView(selection:content:) with tabItem(_:), tag(_:) and badge(_:)
summary: The standard TabView: three to five top-level destinations in the system tab bar, with the theme's accent as the selected colour. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For the top-level areas of an app that people switch between constantly. Give each tab a Label with a short title and an SF Symbol.
whenNotToUse: For views of one screen's content use MonarchTabs (see tabs). For more than five destinations, or on an iPad, use a sidebar (see sidebar-nav).
api: func tabItem(_ label: () -> some View) -> some View
func tag(_ tag: some Hashable) -> some View
func badge(_ count: Int) -> some View

states.name: selected
states.description: The tab's symbol and title take the tint, and the system uses the filled variant of the symbol.

states.name: badge
states.description: A red system badge with a count or a text on the tab.

appearance: The system draws the bar with its material, above the home indicator. The selected tab takes the tint, which monarchTheme sets to the theme's accent; the badge is the system's red.
platformNotes: The parity map named TabView with Tab. Tab and its builder are iOS 18 API and do not compile against the iOS 17 deployment target, so the entry documents the tabItem form, which works on iOS 17 and later; an app that requires iOS 18 can write Tab("Home", systemImage: "house", value: .home) { … } instead. The web BottomTabBar draws its own bar with links, an active icon, a badge and badgeLabel, safe-area padding, a fixed position and hideFrom. On iOS the bar, the insets, the filled active symbol and the badge are the system's, and tabs are views, not links. Android uses the Material NavigationBar.
accessibility: System behaviour: the bar is a tab bar; each item is read with its title, "tab", its position and whether it is selected.
System behaviour: a badge is read with the tab ("3 items").
System behaviour: touching and holding the bar shows a large version of the item for people using large text.
Give every tab a title. An image without a title has no name.
edgeCases: More than five tabs on a phone become a More tab; keep to five.
Each tab keeps its own state, so put a NavigationStack inside each tab, not around the TabView.
The tab bar's titles do not scale with Dynamic Type; the system's large-content viewer covers that.

examples.title: Four destinations and a More button
examples.webExample: Four destinations and a More button
examples.template:
TabView(selection: $tab) {
    Text({{items.0.label}})
        .monarchTextStyle(.title)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .monarchCanvas()
        .tabItem { Label({{items.0.label}}, systemImage: "house") }
        .tag({{items.0.key}})
    Text({{items.1.label}})
        .monarchTextStyle(.title)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .monarchCanvas()
        .tabItem { Label({{items.1.label}}, systemImage: "tray") }
        .badge({{items.1.badge}})
        .tag({{items.1.key}})
    Text({{items.2.label}})
        .monarchTextStyle(.title)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .monarchCanvas()
        .tabItem { Label({{items.2.label}}, systemImage: "magnifyingglass") }
        .tag({{items.2.key}})
    Text({{items.3.label}})
        .monarchTextStyle(.title)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .monarchCanvas()
        .tabItem { Label({{items.3.label}}, systemImage: "bell") }
        .tag({{items.3.key}})
    Text({{items.4.label}})
        .monarchTextStyle(.title)
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .monarchCanvas()
        .tabItem { Label({{items.4.label}}, systemImage: "ellipsis") }
        .tag({{items.4.key}})
}
.frame(minHeight: 240)
